title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation tool was used to create sexually explicit synthetic images of a real person without consent. The attacker obtained source photographs from private social media accounts and used the tool to generate obscene morphed images, then distributed them across multiple platforms using fake accounts and anonymous servers to conceal his identity. The deployment failure was the absence of any technical barrier to this misuse, such as verification that the person depicted had consented to generating such images, or detection and reporting of the harmful content once distributed.

The system enabled non-consensual intimate image abuse at scale. The victim only learned of the abuse when contacted by strangers, showing that the platforms hosting the images had no effective moderation. What would have caught this earlier was either consent verification at the point of image generation, platform monitoring to detect synthetic intimate abuse material, or both.

It is not established whether the AI tool's terms of service prohibited this use, or what measures the tool's operator had deployed to prevent it.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing sexually explicit images using artificial intelligence technology. He obtained photographs of a 22-year-old college acquaintance from her private social media accounts and used AI tools to generate obscene morphed images. Bansal operated multiple fake accounts across Instagram, Discord, and Facebook, along with several Gmail addresses, to hide his identity while uploading and sharing the harmful content through anonymous servers.

The victim discovered the images when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her morphed photographs and videos were circulating on Discord servers. She reported the matter to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During the investigation, police analyzed digital evidence and traced the fake profiles back to Bansal. He admitted knowing the complainant from college and stated that personal resentment from repeated insults motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with further investigation ongoing.
